title: Tree-Based Pseudo-LRU (8-way)
constraints: 7 tree bits in heap order: `bits[0]` is the root. Node n has children 2n+1 (left) and 2n+2 (right). Nodes 3–6 each choose between two adjacent ways (node 3: ways 0/1, …, node 6: ways 6/7).
**Victim:** walk from the root. At each node, bit 0 means go left and bit 1 means go right.
**Update** (rising edge with `touch = 1`): set every node on the path to `way` so that it points **away** from `way` (1 if `way` is in the left subtree, 0 if in the right).
Synchronous reset clears all bits (so `victim = 0`). `bits` exposes the state. Must be synthesizable.
hints: The three bits of `way` are exactly the path: `way[2]` picks the root's side, `way[1]` the next level, `way[0]` the last.
Path nodes for way w: root 0, then `1 + w[2]`, then `3 + w[2:1]`.
Each node on the path gets the **inverse** of the direction taken: `bits[0] <= !w[2]`, and so on.

examples.title: round robin fill
examples.input: touch ways in victim order 8 times
examples.expected: every way is chosen exactly once
